questions.question: What should the next piece of work after OP-01's record be, given the research's rule that the record-derived check set must be written before any spec exists?

options.label: RFC first (Recommended)
options.description: Write an RFC that amends RFC-0024 step 5 and 6 with the research: Pipeline A's order (records-only check set before the spec), the gates worth adopting now, and how step 6's bake-off relates to the research's trial. It needs the research brought into sdd/research. Nothing on OP-01 is built until it lands, so the ordering can't be lost by accident.

options.label: Reopen OP-01 first
options.description: Run the reopen session on O14 to O44 so the record is settled and can be frozen at a hash. The spec, the check set and any trial all need that anyway. The process question stays open for now.

options.label: Check set now, spec later
options.description: Write OP-01's record-derived check set in a records-only session under the /observe-style read scope before anything else, for the decisions no open item blocks. Keeps the ordering, but commits to Pipeline A before an RFC decides it.

options.label: Spec as RFC-0024 says
options.description: Write OP-01's spec for the unblocked clauses, as step 5 says today. Fastest, but it gives up a spec-blind check set for OP-01, the central measurement the research says is missing.

questions.question: Should I also read the research notes in full (about 136k words across 20 files) before we design anything, or are the reports enough?

options.label: Reports suffice (Recommended)
options.description: The reports carry the notes' recommendation IDs and figures. I'd open a specific note only when a decision rests on one claim, for example D1-R1's wheat count or the trial's O-criteria.

options.label: Read all notes now
options.description: Read all of them, via parallel subagents that each return the claims relevant to OP-01. Costs a large token budget, and a subagent's summary loses detail too.

options.label: Only D1, D4, D5
options.description: Read only the notes behind wheats and chaffs, G4a and expectation independence, the three that would shape an OP-01 pipeline. About 18k words.

questions.question: What should this session (obs2spec) produce from the research and the handover?

options.label: RFC amending 0024 (Rec.)
options.description: One RFC that brings the research into sdd/research, amends RFC-0024 steps 5 and 6 (adopt-now gates, record checks before freeze, trial as a step, bake-off reconciled) and files the backlog items it creates. Binding process change, reviewed via /ship or /pr.

options.label: Backlog items only
options.description: File the prerequisites and decisions as BK items under BK-485's dossier and change no process yet. Cheaper, but RFC-0024 step 5 stays as written, so the next session may write OP-01's spec in the old order.

options.label: Record-quality brief first
options.description: Write the next research brief (record completeness and consistency) for the research repo now, and do the RFC after it returns. Delays any process change by one research run.

questions.question: How should OP-01's real spec (RFC-0024 step 5) be ordered relative to the trial?

options.label: After freeze, parallel (Rec.)
options.description: Order: record checks, then reopen O14 to O44, then freeze. After the freeze, OP-01's spec is written by the normal flow alongside the trial, with E authors read-scoped away from it. Adopt-now gates (G0, G3) apply to it. Risk: a later trial result may change the gates.

options.label: After the trial
options.description: Hold OP-01's spec until the core-tier trial reports. Its gates are then measured, not assumed, but spec work waits roughly 80+ hours of trial plus Stage 0.

options.label: Unblocked clauses now
options.description: Write spec clauses for decisions no open item blocks, before the freeze. Fastest, but spec text then exists before any record-derived check set, the order the research warns against.

questions.question: Is an independent second rater (the handover's P2, about 50 h of labelling and seeding) available for the trial?

options.label: No: single-rater pilot
options.description: The trial is framed up front as a single-rater pilot, and every label-dependent measure (realism rating, judge precision, register auto-labels) is marked unvalidated.

options.label: Yes, a person exists
options.description: An external person can do the seeding and labelling, so the human seeder stays blind to the families and gates as the protocol requires.

options.label: Undecided, record open
options.description: Leave D1 as an open point in the RFC, blocking the pre-registration commit but not Stage 0 or the record work.

questions.question: Where should the trial's harness, seeds, labels, analysis scripts and pre-registration live (handover P3)?

options.label: remote-store repo (Rec.)
options.description: Next to the records and the /observe hook it reuses for read scopes. Needs a placement under AUTHORING.md (e.g. a trials/ area) and keeps the 90 M-token runs' artefacts beside the specs they test.

options.label: Dedicated repo
options.description: Keeps trial code, seeds and large run outputs out of remote-store's tree and gates. The hook and record files must then be vendored or pinned by hash.

questions.question: Which scope should the RFC that amends RFC-0024 take?

options.label: New item, full RFC (Rec.)
options.description: A new BK item hosting RFC-0029 and sdd/research/research-spec-faithfulness.md (the external reports pinned at fc762e6). It amends RFC-0024 § 9 steps 5 and 6: record checks, then OP-01's reopen, then the freeze; the spec written after the freeze in parallel with the trial; adopt-now gates; single-rater pilot; trial home in this repo. It files follow-ups for record checks, the OP-01 reopen, the Stage 0 dry run and the pre-registration. F1 to F6 stay with the format RFC, O21 with the reopen session and BK-436, D10 with BK-489.

options.label: Same, under BK-485
options.description: The same RFC and research doc, tracked under BK-485 as RFC-0024 itself was, with no new item. Fewer IDs, but BK-485's entry, already long, gains another strand. RFC-0026 to 0028 each got their own item.

options.label: Ordering only, trial later
options.description: The RFC fixes only the order (record checks, reopen, freeze, spec) and the adopt-now gates. The trial's own decisions (toolchain, tier, Pipeline C reading, pre-registration) wait for a second RFC after the Stage 0 dry run measures its costs. Smaller now, two RFCs overall.

questions.question: RFC-0024 step 6 plans a bake-off: one set of OP-01 decisions, written once as normative prose and once in the F1 to F6 form; fresh agents implement against each; scored on mutants killed and guarantees invented. The research's trial measures whether record-derived oracles catch spec misreadings. How should the two relate?

options.label: Trial first, bake-off after (Rec.)
options.description: Step 6 becomes the core-tier trial on frozen OP-01. The bake-off follows on the same frozen record and reuses the trial's harness, seeds and mutants. The format RFC waits for both. Slower to the format RFC, but the bake-off is then scored with an oracle the trial has validated.

options.label: Bake-off first, trial after
options.description: Keep step 6 as written, so the format RFC lands sooner. The trial follows as a new step 7. The bake-off's mutant scoring then rests on unvalidated oracles, the gap the research names.

options.label: Merge into one run
options.description: One pre-registered run varies both form and oracle source. It shares the harness and halves the sessions, but two factors at n = 60 with a single rater blur both answers.

questions.question: Which trial tier does the RFC commit to (handover D4)?

options.label: Core tier, A only (Rec.)
options.description: Pipeline A only, H1 to H3, n = 60 seeds, about 80 h and about 90 M tokens (the research's unmeasured estimate, which Stage 0 replaces with measured values). Pipelines B and C′ come later as descriptive extensions. Fits a single-rater pilot.

options.label: Full tier, A + B + C′
options.description: About 136 h and 256 M tokens. It compares pipelines descriptively, though the research says n = 60 cannot rank them, and one rater labels three times the output.

options.label: Stage 0 only, tier later
options.description: The RFC commits only to the toy-operation dry run that measures costs. The tier is decided in an amendment once real hours and tokens are known.

questions.question: Toolchain for the trial's reference model and checks (handover D2 and D3)? The repo already compiles Dafny oracles to Python via Docker and plans an ITF replayer (BK-461), which the external research did not know.

options.label: Python core, Docker extras (Rec.)
options.description: The trial's R and its gates are pure Python: Hypothesis state machine, runtime contracts, CrossHair advisory only. History checks use Porcupine (Go) in Docker, like dafny_verify.sh. Existing Dafny and TLA+ layers stay under SPEC-DESIGN.md and are not part of the trial.

options.label: Pure Python only
options.description: No other runtime, so history checks use detangle (one release, unbenchmarked) after a seeded calibration. Simplest to run, but the weakest history oracle.

options.label: Include Dafny → Python
options.description: Add literal Pipeline C on the repo's existing Dafny-to-Python path, with a back-end DRT leg. This makes the core trial larger, and the research found 9 soundness bugs in Dafny back-ends, Python among them.

questions.question: The handover's record-level checks (tables complete and disjoint, response existence, the added-commitment probe on records) must run before OP-01 is frozen. How do they come about?

options.label: Extend /observe-review (Rec.)
options.description: A deterministic script checks the record's case and state tables (G3) inside /observe-review, which already owns record review (RFC-0028). It runs on OP-01 before the reopen. A research brief on record quality is filed as a follow-up, with RFC-0028 as its baseline. Fast, and builds on what exists.

options.label: Research brief first
options.description: Run the handover's D6 research on record completeness and consistency before building anything. OP-01's reopen and freeze wait for it, and with them the trial.

options.label: Manual pass, tool later
options.description: One audit pass checks OP-01's tables by hand before the reopen; a tool and the research brief come as follow-ups. Quickest for OP-01, but the next record has no check.

questions.question: Which mechanisms should bind OP-01's spec flow now, before any trial result (handover D5, filtered for this repo)?

options.label: G3 + two test rules (Rec.)
options.description: Binding now: G3, tables checked complete and disjoint, one script shared by record and spec tables. Membership predicates wherever a clause leaves the outcome open. Every relaxed comparison also run unrelaxed. Held until the trial: wheat/chaff gating (G2), the per-family kill (G8), LLM judges. Typed non-commitment (G0) stays with the format RFC, which owns F3's terms.

options.label: Also G0 typed lint
options.description: As above, plus a G0 lint requiring each non-commitment to carry one of F3's types. It enforces F3's terms before the format RFC adopts them, which RFC-0024 § R4 leaves to step 6.

options.label: Also G4a per edit
options.description: As the first option, plus per-operation response existence (G4a, medium confidence, own toy trial only). It needs an SMT encoding of OP-01's clauses before the spec settles, a large build for an unmeasured gate.

questions.question: Where in this repo should the trial's harness, seeds, labels, analysis scripts and pre-registration live?

options.label: sdd/research/<id>-trial/ (Rec.)
options.description: A research subfolder, as bk-484-key-model/ holds its spike and probes and token-usage/ its scripts. Outside src/ and tests/, so no gate treats it as product code. The pre-registration is a README.md in it, frozen by its commit hash.

options.label: New top-level trials/
options.description: A dedicated root folder for experiment code, separate from sdd/ documents. AUTHORING.md needs a new placement row and every gate a decision whether to scan it.

options.label: tests/trials/ + sdd doc
options.description: Harness under tests/ so it runs with pytest, and the pre-registration under sdd/research/. Its 90 M-token runs would then sit beside the product suite and its gates.

questions.question: What status does the RFC carry when its PR merges?

options.label: Accepted at merge (Rec.)
options.description: As RFC-0026 to RFC-0028: the PR's review settles it, and RFC-0024 gains an 'Amended by' line in the same PR. Follow-up items are filed open.

options.label: Proposed, accept later
options.description: It merges as Proposed, and RFC-0024 is amended in a later PR once Stage 0 has measured costs. Meanwhile step 5's order is not binding, so OP-01's spec could still be written first.

questions.question: What status does the RFC carry when its PR merges?

options.label: Accepted at merge (Rec.)
options.description: As RFC-0026 to RFC-0028: the PR's review settles it, and RFC-0024 gains an 'Amended by' line in the same PR. Follow-up items are filed open.

options.label: Proposed, accept later
options.description: It merges as Proposed, and RFC-0024 is amended in a later PR once Stage 0 has measured costs. Meanwhile step 5's order is not binding, so OP-01's spec could still be written first.

questions.question: Which mechanisms should bind OP-01's spec flow now, before any trial result (handover D5, filtered for this repo)?

options.label: G3 + two test rules (Rec.)
options.description: Binding now: G3, tables checked complete and disjoint, one script shared by record and spec tables. Membership predicates wherever a clause leaves the outcome open. Every relaxed comparison also run unrelaxed. Held until the trial: wheat/chaff gating (G2), the per-family kill (G8), LLM judges. Typed non-commitment (G0) stays with the format RFC, which owns F3's terms.

options.label: Also G0 typed lint
options.description: As above, plus a G0 lint requiring each non-commitment to carry one of F3's types. It enforces F3's terms before the format RFC adopts them, which RFC-0024 § R4 leaves to step 6.

options.label: Also G4a per edit
options.description: As the first option, plus per-operation response existence (G4a, medium confidence, own toy trial only). It needs an SMT encoding of OP-01's clauses before the spec settles, a large build for an unmeasured gate.

questions.question: Where in this repo should the trial's harness, seeds, labels, analysis scripts and pre-registration live?
